Afterward, tell a trusted Christian, find a Bible-teaching church, and begin reading the Gospel of John.

questions.q: How can I know I am saved?
questions.a: Your assurance rests on God's promises, not on your feelings. If you have turned from sin and trusted Jesus as your Lord and Savior, Scripture says you have eternal life (John 5:24) and that God wants you to know it (1 John 5:13). Jesus promises that no one can snatch you out of His hand (John 10:28). Over time, you will also see signs of new life: a growing love for God, a desire to obey Him, and sorrow over sin (2 Corinthians 5:17). If doubts come, go back to what Jesus has done, not what you have done.

needs.prayer: Father, I come to You honestly. I have sinned against You, and I cannot make myself right with You. I am sorry, and I turn away from my sin. I believe Jesus is Your Son, that He died on the cross for my sins, and that You raised Him from the dead. I trust in Him alone to save me. Thank You for Your grace and forgiveness. Jesus, I receive You as my Lord and Savior. Come into my life, make me new, and fill me with Your Holy Spirit. Help me follow You every day. In Jesus' name, amen.

needs.title: Strength
needs.heading: Bible Verses for Strength
needs.metaTitle: Bible Verses for Strength When Weak
needs.intro: When you are running on empty, His strength is not.

verses.text: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
verses.note: When you wait on the Lord, He renews your strength. He can lift you above weariness and help you keep walking without giving up.

verses.text: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
verses.note: God gives power to the faint and increases strength for those who have none. Feeling empty is not a barrier to His help.

verses.text: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
verses.note: God's grace is enough for you, and His power works most clearly through your weakness. You do not have to pretend to be strong.

verses.text: I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
verses.note: Paul learned that Christ strengthens him for every situation, in plenty or in need. Christ can give you what you need for today too.

verses.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
verses.note: God is a safe place to hide and a source of strength, always near when trouble comes. You can run to Him in the middle of the storm.

verses.text: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
verses.note: Even when your body and heart fail, God remains the strength of your heart. He is your portion when everything else falls short.

verses.text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
verses.note: God promises to be with you, strengthen you, help you, and hold you up with His righteous hand. You are not facing this alone.

verses.text: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.”
verses.note: Joy that comes from God gives you strength. Even in a season of sorrow, delighting in who He is can steady and sustain you.

verses.text: Yahweh is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I will thank him.
verses.note: The Lord is your strength and shield. When you trust Him, He helps you, and your heart can find reasons to thank Him.

verses.text: Finally, be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his might.
verses.note: You are called to be strong in the Lord, drawing on His mighty power rather than your own limited reserves.

verses.text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
verses.note: Jesus invites everyone who is worn out and weighed down to come to Him. He offers real rest for your soul.

verses.text: the God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect?
verses.note: God is the one who equips you with strength and makes your way secure. Your ability to stand comes from Him.

verses.text: Yahweh, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places. For the music director, on my stringed instruments.
verses.note: Even when circumstances are bleak, the Lord is your strength. He makes your feet sure, like a deer on high and rocky places.

verses.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”
verses.note: God told Joshua to be strong and courageous because He would be with him everywhere. That same presence goes with you.

verses.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for Yahweh your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
verses.note: You can be strong and courageous because God Himself goes with you. He will not fail you or abandon you.

verses.text: Yahweh will give strength to his people. Yahweh will bless his people with peace.
verses.note: The Lord gives strength to His people and blesses them with peace. Strength and peace are both gifts He wants to give you.

verses.text: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
verses.note: Fear does not come from God. Through His Spirit He gives you power, love, and self-control to face what is in front of you.

verses.text: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth.
verses.note: When you look around for help, remember where it truly comes from. Your help comes from the Lord who made heaven and earth.

verses.text: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
verses.note: The Lord is your light, your salvation, and the strength of your life. With Him on your side, fear loses its grip.

verses.text: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
verses.note: Paul prays that God would strengthen you with power through His Spirit in your inner being. God strengthens you from the inside out.

verses.text: strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, for all endurance and perseverance with joy,
verses.note: God's glorious might gives you endurance and patience, and even joy, so you can keep going through long and difficult seasons.

verses.text: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.
verses.note: Even as your outward strength fades, God renews your inner life day by day. Do not lose heart.

verses.text: In the day that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul.
verses.note: When you call on God, He answers and puts strength in your soul. Bring Him your need today and expect His help.

verses.text: Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
verses.note: Keep seeking the Lord and His strength, again and again. Turning to Him daily is how you draw on His power.

needs.directAnswer: The Bible says real strength comes from God, not from yourself. When you are tired, weak, or overwhelmed, God promises to renew you, uphold you, and be your refuge. His grace is enough, and His power shows up most clearly in your weakness. You can lean on Him and keep going one day at a time.
needs.versesQuestion: Which Bible verses give strength when you are weak?
needs.versesIntro: These Bible verses about strength remind you that God gives power to the weary and help to the weak. Read them slowly, and let them turn your eyes from your own limits to His.

questions.q: How do I pray for strength when I am exhausted?
questions.a: Be honest with God about how tired you are. You do not need polished words, because He already knows your limits. Tell Him what feels too heavy, then ask Him plainly for strength for the next step, not the whole journey. Pray a verse back to Him, such as Isaiah 40:29 or Psalm 73:26, and thank Him for being near. Then take care of yourself practically: rest, eat, and let others help carry the load. Waiting on God (Isaiah 40:31) often looks like small, daily moments of trust while He renews you.

questions.q: What does it mean that God's strength is made perfect in weakness?
questions.a: In 2 Corinthians 12:9, Paul had asked God three times to remove a painful burden. God answered that His grace was enough, and that His power is seen most fully in weakness. This means your weakness is not a disqualification. When you cannot rely on your own ability, you depend on God, and His strength becomes clear in your life. It does not mean God enjoys your pain. It means He is present and at work in it, carrying you through what you could never carry alone.

needs.prayer: Father, I am tired, and I have come to the end of my own strength. Thank You that Your grace is enough for me. I bring You my weakness and ask You to fill it with Your power. Renew my strength as I wait on You. Lift my heart when it is heavy and steady my steps when I feel like giving up. Help me rest in You instead of striving on my own. Be my refuge today, and give me what I need for the next step. I trust You to carry me. In Jesus' name, amen.

firstTimePrayer.title: How to Pray for the First Time
firstTimePrayer.intro: Prayer is simply talking with God. You do not need special words, a church building, or a perfect life. God already knows you and He wants to hear from you.
steps: Find a quiet spot and take a slow breath. Tell God, "I am here."
Be honest. Tell Him what you are feeling, even if it is doubt or fear.
Thank Him for one thing, however small.
Ask Him for what you need, and for what someone you love needs.
Close in the name of Jesus, the One who opens the way to the Father.
firstTimePrayer.salvationIntro: If you have never asked Jesus to be your Savior, you can do that right now. There is nothing magic about these words. What matters is your heart. If you mean it, pray this:
firstTimePrayer.salvationPrayer: Father, I come to You as I am. I know I have sinned and I cannot fix that on my own. I believe Jesus is Your Son, that He died on the cross for my sins, and that You raised Him from the dead. Jesus, I ask You to forgive me and to be the Lord of my life. I receive Your gift of grace. Fill me with Your Holy Spirit and help me follow You every day. Thank You for loving me and bringing me home. In Jesus' name, amen.
firstTimePrayer.afterPrayer: If you prayed that prayer, welcome to the family of God. Tell someone you trust, find a Bible-teaching church near you, and start reading the Gospel of John. We would love to hear from you too.
